source.title: Deep networks on toroids: removing symmetries reveals the structure of flat regions in the landscape geometry
source.authors: Fabrizio Pittorino; A. Ferraro; Gabriele Perugini; Christoph Feinauer; Carlo Baldassi; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: Text includes the paper and appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Measures local training-error flatness and test error across solutions found by different optimization procedures, testing their association with generalization using a different flatness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper studies flatness and generalization, not random-label memorization, architecture comparisons, optimizer generalization in isolation, or dropout. Reported test-error values for the binary models appear in figure legends; local-energy values are figure-only. The paper describes the correlations in text.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 measures training-error increases under weight-magnitude-scaled Gaussian perturbations and relates them to test error in convolutional networks with near-zero training error. This tests V7's correlation component using a different flatness statistic.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors report a correlation between wider minima and better generalization, and argue that symmetry removal reveals connectivity and distance patterns consistent with an octopus-shaped organization of solutions. Their evidence is numerical and correlational.
record.recipe_differences: Uses local training-error energy under multiplicative Gaussian weight perturbations for continuous networks and random sign flips for binary networks; it compares solutions found by SGD, RSGD and adversarial initialization rather than testing the claim's specified measure.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that flatness and generalization vary by solution-finding algorithm (RSGD, SGD, ADV); their local-energy measure uses different perturbations for continuous and binary networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Continuous fully connected MLPs also show the reported correlation between relative-weight perturbation robustness and test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Magnitude-scaled perturbation robustness correlates with generalization in fully connected networks with near-zero training error.

fits_no_version.finding: Binary committee machines and binary MLPs show associations among sign-flip robustness, test error and path barriers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In binary fully connected networks, robustness to random weight-sign flips correlates with lower test error.

record.problems: The paper notes its sampling is very limited for distance results. The reported local-energy and test-error curves are primarily figures, and the text does not give their exact values for the continuous-weight models. Results establish correlation, not causation.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant separately stated results omitted. Figure-only local-energy values are not reconstructed; rows record qualitative results stated in the text and exact test-error legend values where provided.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison; random labels are used for adversarial initialization.
No width sweep of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained to convergence past interpolation; binary width and input-dimension sweeps use different systems.
No isolated test of local connectivity, learned sparse connections, or convolution-derived initialization. The extracted rows do not establish a matched architecture comparison.
No matched adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under the specified tuning conditions.

No ranking against norm- or margin-based measures, no SVHN experiment, and no demonstration of similarly low objective loss. The continuous statistic measures average error increase at fixed noise amplitudes rather than the maximum tolerated perturbation. Test error serves as an approximate gap comparison because training errors are below 1%.
No removal of highly memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Different flatness definitions and untested comparator rankings do not themselves warrant limits_scope. The binary and continuous results do not establish causation.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report held-out accuracy for random labels versus natural labels under the same training recipe.
No sweep of width past the zero-training-error threshold in continuous one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on matched image tasks.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for held-out performance under matched tuning.
Does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness with norm- and margin-based measures or test the stated ranking against those measures. The reported association is correlational.
Does not remove influential memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: Fully connected binary committee machine
rows.size_stated: hidden layer size H = 101; input size N varied
rows.operation_detail: Measured local energy, generalization error and maximum error along random linear paths as overparameterization increased.
rows.measure: Relationship of local energy and test error; maximum path error additionally reported
rows.value: As parameters increase, flatness increases and generalization error is correlated with flatness; average maximum path error decreases.
rows.note: The reported test-error values are plotted; the text describes the correlation without listing the numbers.
rows.check: A binary committee machine on synthetic data does not test V7's convolutional-network comparison. Local-energy correlation and path-barrier results should also be separate measures.

rows.subject: Binary MLP with 3 hidden layers
rows.operation_detail: Measured binary-weight local energy and compared it with test errors for ADV, SGD and RSGD solutions.
rows.measure: Local energy and test error across solution types
rows.value: Test errors: ADV (11.6±0.1%), SGD (10.8±0.2%), RSGD (10.2±0.1%); text says average barrier height correlates with local energy, which in turn correlates with test errors.
rows.uncertainty: ±0.1%, ±0.2%, and ±0.1% as reported for the respective test errors.
rows.note: The figure legend gives the test-error values; the text reports the qualitative correlation.
rows.check: This is a fully connected binary MLP using random sign-flip robustness. Appendix B also says the nominal SGD and RSGD conditions actually use Adam; ADV uses SGD.

rows.measure: Local energy and test error across solution types
rows.value: Test errors: ADV (50.5±0.4%), SGD (46.7±0.1%), RSGD (45.8±0.2%); text says average barrier height correlates with local energy, which in turn correlates with test errors.
rows.uncertainty: ±0.4%, ±0.1%, and ±0.2% as reported for the respective test errors.
rows.note: The figure legend gives the test-error values; the text reports the qualitative correlation.
rows.check: Binary weights have equal magnitude, so sign flips provide a discrete relative-weight perturbation test of the correlation component. Correct the optimizer conditions: nominal SGD uses Adam for 400 epochs; RSGD uses replicated Adam for 300; ADV uses random-label SGD initialization followed by Adam for 200. The reported test-error values are correct.
